title: Emil's Weekly Strength, Muscle and Longevity Protocol

days.label: Monday
days.intent: Bench is always first. Build the week around crisp, submaximal strength work with one to two repetitions still available.

items.d: Start easy, then gradually build effort.
Brief bench and squat preparation sets.
1–2 RIR · Rest 2½–3 min · Controlled descent and brief chest pause.
Move directly to the next exercise.

days.cue: Earn the load increase with four clean sets. Leave the gym ready to train again Wednesday.

days.label: Tuesday
days.generatorLabel: Generate optional short HIIT — replaces Zone 2
days.generatorHint: Occasional · recovered weeks · never added on top of Zone 2
days.generatorGoal: Use this occasionally when clearly recovered, not as a weekly quota. The generated session replaces Tuesday Zone 2 and takes 25–35 minutes including warm-up and cooldown.
days.intent: Zone 2 is the permanent and more common choice. A short generated HIIT may occasionally replace it on a two-HIIT week when recovery is clearly good; it is not a weekly quota.

items.d: Start very easy and settle into smooth rhythm.
Speak comfortably in complete sentences. Do not finish hard.
Let breathing and heart rate settle.
Use light support nearby if needed.

days.cue: Given your VO₂ max, choose Zone 2 more often than Tuesday HIIT. Never combine them. If Wednesday deadlift warm-ups feel unusually heavy, perform only two deadlift working sets that week.

days.label: Wednesday
days.intent: Deadlift leads. Overhead press stays assistance work so Friday's paused bench remains protected.

items.d: 10 glute bridges · 6 reverse lunges/leg · 10 wall slides or band pull-aparts.
Build to the working load without fatigue.
2 RIR · Rest 2½–3 min · Keep all five sets technically consistent.
Assistance work; do not chase numbers at Friday's expense.

items.n: Pendlay row or one-arm dumbbell row

items.d: Heavy enough to challenge posture, but stop before grip failure.

days.cue: Keep the press honest and repeatable. Friday's bench is the priority.

days.label: Thursday
days.generatorHint: Rower preferred · SkiErg occasional · Friday-bench safe
days.generatorGoal: The generated session replaces the complete Norwegian 4 × 4 session. Do not combine them. Prefer rower-led alternatives; use SkiErg occasionally when it better suits leg recovery.
days.intent: Norwegian 4 × 4 on the rower is the permanent default. Use SkiErg occasionally when useful, or use the alternative generator for a deliberate variety week.

items.d: Prefer the rower most weeks. Include three brief 10-second accelerations.
Use the rower by default. Approximately RPE 8–9/10; keep the final interval close to the first interval's output.
Keep moving and let output settle before the next effort.

days.cue: Choose exactly one: Norwegian 4 × 4 or a generated alternative. A loaded CrossFit workout may replace the session, but then omit Friday front squats.

days.label: Friday
days.intent: A second precise bench exposure plus efficient hypertrophy work. If Saturday will be an interval run, omit front squats—do not relocate them.

items.d: Prepare the pause and working groove.
One clear chest pause · 2 RIR · Rest 2–2½ min.
2 RIR · Rest ~2 min · Omit before a Saturday interval run.
Add weight once 10 controlled reps are comfortable · Rest 75–90 sec.

items.n: Incline dumbbell curl or hammer curl

days.cue: Own every pause. Monday and Friday progress independently.

days.label: Saturday
days.intent: An equipment-free conversational run. Keep the first ten minutes deliberately easy.

items.d: Keep the first 10 minutes deliberately easy.

days.cue: No equipment and no interval obligation. Preserve the recovery runway into Monday bench.

days.label: Sunday
days.intent: No structured exercise is required. Sunday should improve Monday's bench readiness.
days.cue: Recovery is training when it protects the next high-quality session.

TUESDAY_SHORT.title: Rower · Six Sharp Minutes
TUESDAY_SHORT.tagline: The preferred Tuesday HIIT option: concise, measurable, and low in muscle damage.

moves.name: Progressive row
moves.detail: Easy strokes building to two brief accelerations.

moves.name: Hard row
moves.detail: RPE 8–9 with repeatable watts; never sprint to failure.

moves.name: Easy row
moves.detail: Very light pressure and relaxed breathing.

moves.name: Cooldown
moves.detail: Easy strokes until breathing is calm.

notes: This replaces Tuesday Zone 2; do not add it afterward.
Use only when recovered; Zone 2 remains the more common Tuesday choice.
Wednesday deadlift warm-ups decide whether to use two or three working sets.

TUESDAY_SHORT.title: Rower · Forty-Five / Seventy-Five
TUESDAY_SHORT.tagline: Fast enough to lift output, short enough to avoid a deep fatigue hole.

moves.name: Easy row
moves.detail: Keep the flywheel moving without chasing distance.

notes: Hold output across all eight efforts.
No strength work is added to this session.
Finish with energy still in reserve for Wednesday.

TUESDAY_SHORT.title: Rower · Ten Clean Thirties
TUESDAY_SHORT.tagline: Short power exposures with generous recovery and minimal residual fatigue.

moves.name: Progressive row
moves.detail: Easy to moderate, then two short accelerations.

moves.name: Hard row
moves.detail: Powerful but technically clean; no all-out final rep.

moves.name: Easy row
moves.detail: Use 60 seconds when output stays level, 90 when needed.

notes: Use the recovery needed to preserve quality.
Do not turn this into a maximal sprint test.
The whole session replaces Zone 2.

TUESDAY_SHORT.title: Rower · Five by Two
TUESDAY_SHORT.tagline: The upper edge of Tuesday's dose without becoming a second primary HIIT day.

moves.name: Progressive row
moves.detail: Build gradually with two brief accelerations.

moves.name: Hard row
moves.detail: RPE 8/10; select a split all five efforts can hold.

notes: Ten hard minutes is Tuesday's ceiling.
Do not add lifting, calisthenics, or Zone 2.
Reduce Wednesday deadlifts to two work sets if warm-ups are unusually heavy.

TUESDAY_SHORT.title: Rower / SkiErg · Alternating Minutes
TUESDAY_SHORT.tagline: A little variety without turning the session into loaded CrossFit.

moves.name: Progressive machine warm-up
moves.detail: Four minutes rower, three minutes SkiErg; both easy.

moves.name: Hard intervals
moves.detail: Alternate rower and SkiErg each round at RPE 8.

moves.name: Easy transition
moves.detail: Move calmly and begin the next machine under control.

moves.name: Cooldown
moves.detail: Use whichever machine feels more restorative.

notes: The rower remains preferable; use SkiErg volume conservatively.
Keep shoulders, lats, and triceps well away from failure.
This replaces Zone 2 rather than supplementing it.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: Rower · Six by Two
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: A primary HIIT dose with shorter repetitions than Norwegian 4 × 4.
notes: This replaces 4 × 4 completely.
Keep all six efforts within a narrow output range.
No barbell work is added.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: SkiErg · Five by Three
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: An occasional lower-leg-load alternative with controlled upper-body volume.

moves.name: Hard SkiErg
moves.detail: RPE 8; tall posture and full strokes.

moves.name: Cooldown
moves.detail: Stop before upper-body fatigue becomes grinding.

notes: This replaces 4 × 4.
Use occasionally: longer SkiErg intervals can fatigue the lats, shoulders, and triceps before Friday bench.
Prefer the rower when both machines are equally suitable.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: Rower / SkiErg · Eight Nineties
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: Alternating machines distributes the primary HIIT dose without loaded strength work.

moves.name: Progressive warm-up
moves.detail: Start on the rower; use the SkiErg portion conservatively, then complete two short accelerations.

moves.name: Hard intervals
moves.detail: Alternate rower and SkiErg; hold RPE 8–9.

moves.name: Easy transition
moves.detail: Move calmly and start each interval ready.

notes: The generated session replaces Norwegian 4 × 4.
Transitions are recovery, not extra work.
Prefer a rower-only alternative if upper-body fatigue could affect Friday bench.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: Rower · Power + Moderate Swings
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: Rower-led conditioning with a small, controlled hinge dose.

moves.name: Kettlebell swings
moves.detail: After each row; crisp hip snap, never heavy or grinding.

moves.name: Easy recovery
moves.detail: Begin after swings; extend slightly if technique needs it.

notes: This is the entire HIIT session and replaces 4 × 4.
The kettlebell must stay moderate.
If swings create meaningful soreness, choose a machine-only option next time.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: SkiErg · Intervals + Light Carries
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: An occasional SkiErg option with posture work that stays clear of muscular failure.

moves.name: Light farmer carry
moves.detail: After each interval; easy posture, no grip grind.

notes: This replaces 4 × 4.
Carries are light support work, not a strength test.
Use occasionally and stop before lat, shoulder, triceps, or grip fatigue affects Friday.

THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.title: Rower · Controlled Burpee Waves
THURSDAY_ALTERNATIVE.tagline: Rower power with deliberately capped bodyweight volume.

moves.name: Burpees
moves.detail: Step or jump smoothly; no maximal pace and no push-up volume target.

notes: Thirty-two total burpees is the cap.
This replaces Norwegian 4 × 4.
Choose a machine-only session if burpees threaten Friday bench quality.

guide.title: Monday bench · 4–6 reps
guide.body: Begin with a load you can complete for 4 × 4 with 1–2 RIR. Add repetitions until all four sets reach 6 clean reps, then add 2.5 kg and return to 4. Fractional plates allowing a 1 kg increase are useful when needed.

guide.title: Friday bench · 6–8 reps
guide.body: Begin with a load you can pause for 4 × 6 at 2 RIR. Progress toward 4 × 8, then add 2.5 kg and return to 6. Monday and Friday earn increases independently.

guide.title: The 100 kg checkpoint
guide.body: When you can bench approximately 87.5 kg × 5 with one clean repetition available, a 100 kg attempt is reasonable. Use a spotter or correctly positioned safeties.

guide.title: Other exercises
guide.body: Reach the top of the prescribed range on every set while maintaining the intended RIR. Add the smallest practical weight, then return to the bottom of the range. Never increase load merely because the calendar says so. Wednesday deadlifts use five sets of five at 2 RIR.

guide.title: HIIT week selection
guide.body: One-HIIT week: Tuesday Zone 2 and Thursday Norwegian 4 × 4. Occasional two-HIIT week: when recovered, Tuesday's short generated HIIT replaces Zone 2 while Thursday remains 4 × 4; this is an option, not an expected weekly quota. Given your VO₂ max, Tuesday Zone 2 should remain the more common choice. Variety week: Tuesday Zone 2 and Thursday's generated primary HIIT replaces 4 × 4.

guide.title: Tuesday autoregulation
guide.body: Tuesday HIIT is optional, machine-dominant, and never added to Zone 2. If Wednesday deadlift warm-ups feel unusually heavy after it, perform only two deadlift working sets that week. This is an autoregulation rule, not a separate phase.

guide.title: Loaded CrossFit exception
guide.body: If you deliberately use one of the old loaded CrossFit workouts, use it as Thursday's entire session, omit Norwegian 4 × 4, and omit Friday front squats. Never combine the sessions.

guide.title: Aerobic volume + walking
guide.body: A normal week provides roughly 80–105 minutes of easy aerobic work plus 16 hard interval minutes: approximately 112–137 moderate-equivalent minutes before warm-ups and ordinary walking. This is near the lower longevity threshold. If daily activity is otherwise low, add 20–40 minutes of brisk walking across the week.

guide.title: Fatigue adjustments
guide.body: After two declining sessions: return Tuesday to Zone 2; remove one set from curls, lateral raises, and triceps; if needed, reduce deadlifts to two working sets for that week. Keep the main bench practice unless shoulder or elbow pain is present.

guide.title: Morning nutrition
guide.body: Before: 400–600 ml water; coffee or modest caffeine is optional; electrolytes only when useful. After: eat within about two hours, include 35–45 g protein and carbohydrates—especially after strength and HIIT—and continue toward roughly 150 g daily protein.

guide.title: When performance feels flat
guide.body: Test one banana, 20–30 g whey protein, and water before training. This is optional; keep it only if actual bench or HIIT performance improves.

guide.title: Weekly structure
guide.body: Monday heavy bench and full-body strength · Tuesday Zone 2 or optional short generated HIIT · Wednesday 5 × 5 deadlift, full-body strength, and farmer walk · Thursday Norwegian 4 × 4 or generated primary HIIT · Friday paused bench and hypertrophy · Saturday equipment-free 50–70-minute run · Sunday rest.
